questions.question: Which correction fixes: "It don't look great"?
questions.explanation: With third-person singular subjects like "it", use "doesn't" (does not), not "don't".

questions.question: You wrote: "english-coach-app is builded in ~/project". What is the best fix?
questions.explanation: "Build" is irregular: past participle is "built", not "builded".

questions.question: Which sentence correctly asks about a service at http://127.0.0.1:8123?
questions.explanation: Use "is not running" to describe the current state of a service or server.

questions.question: Which option best improves: "In summary , what is the most mistake I often make?"
options: A. In summary, what most mistake I often make?
B. In summary, what is the mistake I make most often?
C. In summary, what is most common mistake I make?
D. In summary, what is the most mistake I often make?
questions.explanation: Use "the mistake I make most often" or "the most common mistake" — "most mistake" is not grammatical.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct for a feature request?
options: C. Add a quiz every day
questions.explanation: Capitalize the first word, use article "a" before singular countable "quiz", and "every day" is two words when meaning daily.

questions.question: Which fixes the error in: "summarize error occured today"?
questions.explanation: Use the verb "Summarize", possessive "today's errors", and spell "occurred" with double "r" when needed.

questions.question: Translate into natural technical English: "the hook 好像失效了"
questions.modelAnswer: The hook seems to have stopped working.
questions.explanation: Use present perfect or "seems to have stopped working" for a recent change; "失效" in dev contexts is often "stopped working" or "is broken".

questions.question: Translate into English: "Qwen3-8B 是存文本吗" (asking about model capabilities).
questions.explanation: "存文本" in ML context means text-only (no image/multimodal input); "pure text" or "text-only" is standard.

questions.question: Rewrite naturally: "I want install a privite github on this mac"
questions.modelAnswer: I want to install a private GitHub instance on this Mac.
questions.explanation: After "want" use infinitive "to install"; spell "private"; capitalize "GitHub" and "Mac" as proper nouns.

questions.question: Rewrite for a coding agent: "I want you help me to make the code more faster and also fix the bug that is not working correctly"
questions.modelAnswer: I want you to help me make the code faster and fix the bug that isn't working correctly.
questions.explanation: Use "want you to help"; "faster" alone (not "more faster"); "isn't working" is natural for a broken feature.
